{"id": "f2f30669-858c-4186-b190-4ede661170c4", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's the core difference:

**EKS Managed Node Groups**
- Backed by actual EC2 instances (or Spot) that AWS provisions and registers as Kubernetes nodes, grouped in an Auto Scaling group
- You choose instance types, AMI, disk size, and manage scaling (min/max/desired capacity)
- AWS automates provisioning, updates, and graceful draining/termination during upgrades, but you still own node-level config (e.g., custom AMIs, DaemonSets needing node access, GPU workloads)
- Supports all pod types, DaemonSets, privileged pods, and workloads needing specific instance types (GPU, high memory, etc.)
- You pay for the EC2 instances regardless of utilization — bin-packing efficiency matters

**Fargate Profiles**
- Serverless — no EC2 instances to manage at all. Each pod gets its own isolated micro-VM sized to its requests
- You define profiles matching namespaces/labels to determine which pods run on Fargate
- No node management, patching, or capacity planning — AWS handles it entirely
- Billed per pod based on vCPU/memory requested, rounded up to Fargate increments
- Limitations: no DaemonSets, no privileged containers, no GPU support, no EBS volumes (EFS only), and a few networking/storage restrictions

**When to use which**
- Fargate: unpredictable or spiky workloads, teams wanting zero infra management, strict per-pod isolation requirements
- Managed node groups: DaemonSets, GPU/specialized instances, high-density bin-packing for cost efficiency, or workloads needing node-level customization
